title: When to use lines instead of bars

cues.en: Host: In this video I'm going to discuss using line plots versus bar plots to display the same information.
cues.zh: 這部影片討論，使用折線圖或長條圖，顯示相同資訊。

cues.en: And this really relates to an implicit assumption.
cues.zh: 這其實涉及一個隱含假設。

cues.en: Implicit assumption means that there is an assumption that you are imposing on the data, and implicit means you might not realize that you are making that assumption.
cues.zh: 隱含假設，代表你對資料施加某種假設，但可能沒意識到自己在做這個假設。

cues.en: Okay, so let's begin.
cues.zh: 開始吧。

cues.en: Let's go back to these, this bar plot and this histogram that I showed previously in the course.
cues.zh: 回到課程先前展示的長條圖與直方圖。

cues.en: So remember this was how many people get their news from different media sources, and this was the height of different penguins grouped into these bins
cues.zh: 記得，這是從不同媒體取得新聞的人數，這是不同企鵝的身高，分成，

cues.en: of seven centimeters, or sorry, 10 centimeters.
cues.zh: 七公分，抱歉，是十公分的區間。

cues.en: So here are bars and here are bars.
cues.zh: 這裡有長條，這裡也有。

cues.en: Now bars are the right way to show these data in both of these cases.
cues.zh: 兩個例子，用長條呈現都正確。

cues.en: What about if we drew lines between the bars?
cues.zh: 如果在長條間畫線呢？

cues.en: Maybe you say, well it looks nice, nice color, and the lines are a little bit softer on the eyes, and now we can say, well, you know, we're actually showing
cues.zh: 也許你覺得好看，顏色漂亮，線條比較柔和；現在其實是用線與長條，顯示，

cues.en: the same information with the lines and the bars.
cues.zh: 相同資訊。

cues.en: It's redundant information.
cues.zh: 資訊重複了。

cues.en: So why don't we get rid of the bars altogether and just have these lines?
cues.zh: 為什麼不直接拿掉長條，只留線？

cues.en: Well, that's what is the problem here?
cues.zh: 這有什麼問題？

cues.en: Maybe you can pause the video and decide what is, what's wrong with having lines in this graph over here.
cues.zh: 可以暫停，想想這張圖裡，使用線條有什麼不對。

cues.en: So the problem here with lines is that lines make the implicit assumption that a data point measured between our actual data points.
cues.zh: 線條的問題，是隱含假設：在實際資料點之間，若測量一個資料點，

cues.en: So if we had a data point here, then that value would correspond to this location on the Y axis.
cues.zh: 如果這裡有資料點，數值就對應y軸這個位置。

cues.en: So this data point here, if we had measured a data point here on the x axis, then we would expect to see a value of 20% people responding.
cues.zh: 如果在x軸這裡測量資料點，就會預期20%的人回答。

cues.en: But what does that mean?
cues.zh: 但這代表什麼？

cues.en: That doesn't mean any, it doesn't even make sense for this plot.
cues.zh: 對這張圖而言，完全沒意義。

cues.en: What is halfway in between TV and newspaper and how can you know the average of TV and newspaper, how can we expect that to be 20%?
cues.zh: 電視和報紙的正中間是什麼？如何取電視與報紙的平均，又為何預期是20%？

cues.en: That that just doesn't make any sense.
cues.zh: 這完全說不通。

cues.en: So that's why lines are totally inappropriate here.
cues.zh: 所以這裡使用線條，完全不適合。

cues.en: Absolutely inappropriate only bars can be used for categorical data like this in bar plots.
cues.zh: 絕對不適合。長條圖中這種類別資料，只能用長條。

cues.en: However, story changes a little bit.
cues.zh: 不過，情況稍有改變。

cues.en: It softens up a little bit when we get over here to these heights in this histogram plot here.
cues.zh: 到了這裡的身高直方圖，限制稍微放寬。

cues.en: And that's because although we don't measure any data at this particular point here, it is pretty reasonable
cues.zh: 雖然沒有在這個位置測量資料，但相當合理地，

cues.en: to expect that if we had grouped our bins differently, let's say we had twice as many bins, so for this histogram, so maybe we would have another bin that corresponded
cues.zh: 可以預期，如果用不同分箱，例如區間數加倍，也許會多一個區間，對應，

cues.en: to this axis location.
cues.zh: x軸這個位置。

cues.en: It is pretty reasonable to expect that the Y axis, so the height of this bar here, if we did have a bar here,
cues.zh: 合理地可以預期，y軸，也就是若這裡有長條，其高度，

cues.en: would be somewhere around here, 15, 16, 17.
cues.zh: 大概會在15、16、17附近。

cues.en: That's pretty reasonable to expect.
cues.zh: 這是合理的預期。

cues.en: We wouldn't expect based on the shape of this distribution, based on what we know about distributions of heights in general, you wouldn't expect that the real data here would, you don't expect it
cues.zh: 根據分布形狀，以及一般身高分布的知識，不會預期真實資料，

cues.en: to bounce all over the place.
cues.zh: 在這裡到處亂跳。

cues.en: You expect it to be smooth.
cues.zh: 會預期它平滑。

cues.en: So therefore, lines here in a histogram are technically formally by the letter of the statistical laws incorrect,
cues.zh: 所以嚴格遵照統計規則，直方圖這裡用線條，形式上是錯的，

cues.en: but it's not so bad in this case.
cues.zh: 但這個例子沒那麼糟。

cues.en: This is kind of like a soft violation.
cues.zh: 這算輕微違規。

cues.en: This is a really bad violation.
cues.zh: 這則是嚴重違規。

cues.en: Okay, so I'm gonna show two situations where lines can be used instead of bars for a histogram plot.
cues.zh: 接著示範兩種情況，直方圖能用線條代替長條。

cues.en: One is when you have lots and lots of bars like this, and then, so basically you have a fine resolution on the x axis.
cues.zh: 一種是長條非常多，像這樣，基本上x軸解析度很細。

cues.en: You have a lot of bins on the X axis.
cues.zh: x軸上有很多區間。

cues.en: So then it's pretty reasonable to assume that if we would cut this up into more bins, then a data point between this bar and this bar would be somewhere in between them probably
cues.zh: 這時合理地可以假設，如果再切更多區間，這兩個長條之間的資料點，會在兩者之間，

cues.en: around halfway in between them.
cues.zh: 大概在中間位置。

cues.en: So this is one case where it's okay to use lines instead of bars.
cues.zh: 這是一種能用線條代替長條的情況。

cues.en: Another case is if you are comparing multiple data sets in the same graph.
cues.zh: 另一種，是在同一張圖比較多個資料集。

cues.en: So let's say we look at the distribution of heights of king penguins.
cues.zh: 例如看國王企鵝的身高分布。

cues.en: So these are like male king penguins, and I don't actually know if female king penguins are called queen penguins, but I think they should be called
cues.zh: 這些是雄性國王企鵝。我不知道雌性是否叫皇后企鵝，但覺得如果是雌性，

cues.en: queen penguins if they are female.
cues.zh: 就應該叫皇后企鵝。

cues.en: But anyway, let's say that they have this distribution.
cues.zh: 總之，假設它們有這種分布。

cues.en: Now these data, these two distributions would be a little bit harder to interpret if we had two sets of bars instead of two lines.
cues.zh: 如果用兩組長條，而非兩條線，這兩個分布會比較難解讀。

cues.en: And you can imagine if we were comparing multiple different species of penguins, different types of penguins, maybe penguins in different areas of the world,
cues.zh: 可以想像，比較多種企鵝、不同類型，或世界不同地區的企鵝，

cues.en: then we might have like six different lines here, six different groups that we want to compare.
cues.zh: 可能會有六條線，要比較六個不同群體。

cues.en: And having six groups of bars is just totally unreadable.
cues.zh: 六組長條會完全難以閱讀。

cues.en: So this is another case where it's acceptable to use lines instead of bars, and that's when you have a lot of comparisons in the same graph.
cues.zh: 這是另一種可以接受線條取代長條的情況，也就是同一張圖有很多比較。

cues.en: And so bars just become really difficult to interpret.
cues.zh: 長條變得很難解讀。

cues.en: So we switch to lines.
cues.zh: 所以改用線條。

cues.en: So there you go, using lines versus bars.
cues.zh: 以上是線條與長條的使用比較。

cues.en: The short answer is that for bar plots with categorical data, lines are never suitable, lines are never appropriate for bar plots
cues.zh: 簡單說，類別資料的長條圖，線條永遠不適合，

cues.en: with categorical data, for histogram data, for histogram plots, then it's okay, it's technically incorrect to use lines,
cues.zh: 不適合類別資料長條圖。直方圖資料、直方圖，則可以；嚴格來說用線條不正確，

cues.en: but it is often practical to use lines instead of bars.
cues.zh: 但實務上經常適合以線條代替長條。

cues.en: And so it's usually fine as long as you have a good enough resolution of bars so that you can expect that the imaginary points
cues.zh: 所以通常沒問題，只要長條解析度足夠，能預期線上那些，

cues.en: that we didn't measure on the lines actually correspond to what the lines suggest they do.
cues.zh: 未實際測量的虛構點，確實符合線條暗示的值。
